# Low-cost access to orbit

## Scope

In: the cost per kilogram of launch to low Earth orbit, by reusable or otherwise cheaper launch systems. Out: what is built or kept alive in orbit (space/closed-loop-life-support) and in-space transport beyond low Earth orbit.

## Gaps

### Reuse of the whole launch system

severity **high**; status **active**; type cost; layer deployment; blocks Launch cost.

Reusable first stages reduced launch cost, and providers on several continents plan reusable systems. The cost per kilogram falls with cumulative payload launched, following a learning curve, so further reductions depend on reuse at higher rate and with more of the vehicle recovered.

Evidence: [reddy2018spacex](../../evidence/reddy2018spacex.toml), [terzi2026from](../../evidence/terzi2026from.toml).

### Market structure and orbital debris may slow the decline

severity **medium**; status **open**; type regulation; layer deployment; blocks Launch cost.

The study that fits the learning curve warns that geopolitical shifts, possible monopolistic behavior in commercial launch markets and the growing problem of orbital debris may temper the cost reductions.

Evidence: [terzi2026from](../../evidence/terzi2026from.toml).
